title: Computational Proof Systems
description: A study book on zero-knowledge proofs: circuits, R1CS and QAP, polynomial commitments, sum-check, GKR, Groth16, PLONK and lookups, with Rust code.
intro: A rough documentation of the protocols and primitives I explored during my ZK quest, from circuits and polynomials to sum-check, GKR, Groth16 and PLONK. Rust implementations of these protocols are in the [cryptography-n-zk-research](https://github.com/developeruche/cryptography-n-zk-research) repository.

pages.title: Overview of Computation in Zero-Knowledge Proofs
pages.seo_title: From Problem to SNARK: Computation in ZK Proofs
pages.description: How a problem becomes a zero-knowledge proof: computation, algebraic circuits and arithmetization, with a sound Circom IsZero circuit as the example.

pages.title: Arithmetic Circuits
pages.seo_title: Arithmetic Circuits for Zero-Knowledge Proofs
pages.description: What arithmetic circuits are, how their wires and gates compute polynomials over a finite field, and how they differ from Boolean circuits.

pages.title: Arithmetic Circuits in Rust
pages.seo_title: Implementing an Arithmetic Circuit in Rust
pages.description: A layered arithmetic circuit in Rust: the interface, gate and layer data structures, and how evaluation runs from the inputs up to the output.

pages.title: Polynomials
pages.seo_title: Univariate vs Multilinear Polynomials in ZK Proofs
pages.description: The roles of univariate and multilinear polynomials in zero-knowledge proofs: QAP, the Boolean hypercube, commitment schemes and Zeromorph.

pages.title: R1CS to QAP
pages.seo_title: R1CS to QAP: A Complete Worked Example
pages.description: A complete worked example from R1CS to a QAP: the matrices, interpolating each column, combining with the witness, and the final divisibility check.

pages.title: Univariate Polynomial Multiplication Using FFT
pages.seo_title: Polynomial Multiplication Using the FFT
pages.description: Multiplying univariate polynomials with the FFT: evaluate at roots of unity, multiply pointwise, interpolate back, and why fields need roots of unity.

chapters.title: Chapter Two: Interactive and Non-Interactive Proofs

pages.title: Interactive and Non-Interactive Zero-Knowledge Proof Systems
pages.seo_title: Interactive vs Non-Interactive Zero-Knowledge Proofs
pages.description: Interactive and non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs compared: graph 3-coloring, the Fiat-Shamir transform, zk-SNARKs, setup and public verifiability.

pages.title: Polynomial Commitment Schemes
pages.seo_title: Polynomial Commitment Schemes: An Introduction
pages.description: What polynomial commitment schemes are: committing to a polynomial, opening evaluations, and why binding and hiding are different properties.

pages.title: KZG Polynomial Commitment Scheme
pages.seo_title: KZG Polynomial Commitments Explained
pages.description: How KZG works: the SRS, committing, the quotient polynomial, the pairing check, and the costs of its trusted setup.

pages.title: Univariate KZG Polynomial Commitment Scheme
pages.seo_title: Univariate KZG: Worked Example and Rust Code
pages.description: Univariate KZG in practice: recommended resources, a small worked commit, open and verify example, and a Rust implementation.

pages.title: Multilinear KZG Polynomial Commitment Scheme
pages.seo_title: Multilinear KZG Commitments: A Worked Example
pages.description: KZG for multilinear polynomials: the Lagrange-basis SRS, witness polynomials, the pairing check, and a full example worked by hand.

pages.title: Batch Univariate KZG Polynomial Commitment Scheme
pages.seo_title: Batch KZG: Opening at Many Points with One Proof
pages.description: Batch KZG opens one polynomial at several points with a single proof, using an interpolated remainder and a vanishing polynomial. Includes an example.

pages.title: FRI Polynomial Commitment Scheme
pages.seo_title: FRI: A Beginner-Friendly Guide with a Worked Example
pages.description: What FRI is and how it works, in plain language: stretching, Merkle commitments, folding and queries, with a full example you can follow by hand.

pages.title: The Sum-Check Protocol
pages.seo_title: The Sum-Check Protocol: Worked Example and Rust Code
pages.description: The sum-check protocol: each round, a fully worked example by hand, why it is sound, a Rust implementation, and the univariate sum-check.

pages.title: The GKR Protocol
pages.seo_title: The GKR Protocol: Proving Layered Circuits
pages.description: How the GKR protocol proves a layered arithmetic circuit: the layer equation, sum-check reductions, and turning it into a SNARK with a commitment.

pages.title: Succinct GKR Protocol
pages.seo_title: Succinct GKR with Multilinear KZG Commitments
pages.description: Combining GKR with multilinear KZG: committing to the input, what actually gets smaller, a worked example, Rust code and a soundness gap.

pages.title: The Groth16 Protocol
pages.seo_title: The Groth16 Protocol: Setup, Proving and Verifying
pages.description: Groth16 from R1CS and QAP to its trusted setup, the proving key, the three-element proof and the single pairing check that verifies it.

pages.title: The PLONK Protocol
pages.seo_title: The PLONK Protocol: A Guided Walkthrough
pages.description: A guided path through PLONK: the universal setup, Plonkish arithmetization, the prover's five rounds and the verifier's single pairing check.

pages.title: PLONK Introduction and the KZG Universal Setup
pages.seo_title: PLONK and the KZG Universal Trusted Setup
pages.description: An introduction to PLONK and its notation, and how the universal KZG trusted setup works, including which points the structured reference string holds.

pages.title: Plonkish Arithmetization
pages.seo_title: Plonkish Arithmetization and Copy Constraints
pages.description: Plonkish arithmetization by example: the gate equation, selector and witness polynomials, copy constraints, and the permutation argument behind them.

pages.title: The PLONK Prover
pages.seo_title: The PLONK Prover: All Five Rounds Explained
pages.description: The PLONK prover round by round: blinded wires, the permutation polynomial, the quotient, evaluations, linearisation and the two opening proofs.

pages.title: The PLONK Verifier
pages.seo_title: The PLONK Verifier: Step by Step
pages.description: How the PLONK verifier works: replaying the transcript, computing the batched commitments, and the single pairing equation that checks everything.

pages.title: TurboPLONK
pages.seo_title: TurboPLONK: Custom Gates and Transition Constraints
pages.description: TurboPLONK explained: programs as state sequences, transition gates over the next row, selectors for constants, and copy constraints as memory.

pages.title: Lookup Arguments and PlonKup
pages.seo_title: Lookup Arguments in Zero-Knowledge Proofs
pages.description: What lookup arguments are, why they replace many gates with one table check, what they do and don't hide, and how they connect to PLONK.

pages.title: Plookup
pages.seo_title: Plookup: The Lookup Protocol Explained
pages.description: The plookup protocol: sorting values with the table, the aggregation polynomial, the identities the verifier checks, and a small worked example.

pages.title: Halo2 Lookup Protocol
pages.seo_title: The Halo2 Lookup Protocol, with a Worked Example
pages.description: The Halo2 lookup argument with a worked example: permuted columns, the running product, the four checks, and why a cheating prover gets caught.

pages.title: HyperPlonk
pages.seo_title: HyperPlonk: PLONK Without FFTs on the Hypercube
pages.description: A study companion to HyperPlonk: replacing Plonk's FFTs with sum-check over the Boolean hypercube, the zero check, and cheap high-degree gates.

pages.title: Sumcheck 201 Paper Note
pages.seo_title: Sumcheck 201: Collapsing Arrays and Precomputation
pages.description: Notes on Sumcheck 201: the Lagrange basis on the hypercube, the collapsing arrays and precomputation algorithms, and a full three-variable example.

pages.title: Keccak Hash Function
pages.seo_title: Keccak Explained: The Sponge and Keccak-f
pages.description: How Keccak works: the sponge, padding, absorbing and squeezing, the five steps of Keccak-f, and where its one-way security actually comes from.
